messages.author: 8c347bb6aaff118a
messages.subject: Error with paired sample t-tests
parts:
Greetings,

The Confidence Interval calculations are incorrect for the paired
sample t-tests.

Does anyone have a suggestions for a work around?

Thanks,
Roger

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Error with paired sample t-tests
parts:
Please provide the output and code that you think is incorrect, along
with what they should be. I'm doubtful that there is an incorrect
calculation as Deducer is simply calling t.text.


obj_a <- t.test(x = anorexia$Prewt,y = anorexia$Postwt,paired =
TRUE,var.equal=T)
> print(obj_a)

Paired t-test

data: anorexia$Prewt and anorexia$Postwt
t = -2.9376, df = 71, p-value = 0.004458
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
-4.6399424 -0.8878354
sample estimates:
mean of the differences
-2.763889

> rm(obj_a)

messages.subject: Re: Error with paired sample t-tests
parts:
And what do you think that the limits for a one sided confidence
interval should be? Note that your alternate hypothesis is greater
_not_ two-sided. These will give you different intervals.


Ian

messages.author: e8e09c569718008b
messages.subject: Re: Error with paired sample t-tests
parts:
I wondered if this was the problem - specifying a one-sided
alternative hypothesis for a 95% CI. A confidence interval for a
statistic makes the most sense when a two-sided alternative hypothesis
is used, otherwise one of the limits is listed as infinity. Change the
alternative hypothesis to two-sided and things will probably be fine.

Davester
